title: Omission renders as three consecutive visually identical empty periods; the middle one is the omission signature
notes: SOURCE: Hamm, 2026-07-28, direct statement of paradigm structure. Entered as user-asserted design fact, not inference.
Trial structure is always fx - p1 - d1 - p2 - d2 - p3 - d3 - p4 - d4.
p1..p4 carry stimulus identity. fx and d1..d4 are gray screen with fixation dot.
CRITICAL: the delay periods are VISUALLY IDENTICAL to an omission (X). An omitted slot is not a distinct stimulus event — it is indistinguishable on screen from the delays that surround it.
Therefore AAAB renders as  o-A-o-A-o-A-o-B-o  and RRXR renders as  o-R-o-R-o-o-o-R-o.
An omission at slot k produces THREE consecutive visually identical empty periods: d(k-1) + p(k as X) + d(k). For RRXR that is d2 + p3 + d3.
The MIDDLE o — the omitted stimulus slot itself — is where the omission signature must live, because the flanking o's are ordinary delays.
H0: at each channel, in each band, spectral power across the three o's is flat and shows no significant change from baseline.
H1: in at least one band there is a significant positive or negative change from baseline.
These hypotheses are the intended basis of Figures 6, 7 and 8 (three interpretations of the same TFR analysis).

DESIGN CONSEQUENCE: because the flanking o's are visually identical to the middle o, they form a within-trial control that the pre-trial fixation baseline cannot provide. A middle-vs-baseline contrast conflates omission-specific signal with any sustained drift across the trial and with general delay-period state; a middle-vs-flank contrast isolates expectation violation. Both are computed; middle-vs-baseline is primary per Hamm's stated H0, middle-minus-flank is carried as a descriptive robustness column.

TIMING (from domain-paradigm-timing-layout): fx=-500, p1=0, d1=531, p2=1031, d2=1562, p3=2062, d3=2593, p4=3093, d4=3624 ms; stimulus 531 ms, delay 500 ms. Middle-o window = the p<slot> window: slot2 = 1031-1562, slot3 = 2062-2593, slot4 = 3093-3624 ms.

POWER CONSTRAINT observed while implementing: omission-condition TFR files carry a median of 7 trials (min 2, max 85). A per-channel per-band significance test at that trial count has very low power, and 8,736 channels x 5 bands is ~43,680 tests. Per-channel dB effect sizes are reported as requested, but the defensible inferential statement is at session/area level via GLMM, not per-channel significance counts.
issues: map_area_canonical() in the archived census script collapses V3, V3d, V3a into 'V3a-d-v'. The TFR arrays carry them as separate labels (V3 60 files, V3a 60, V3d 60). The V3 alpha/beta exception Hamm reports is averaged away by the manuscript's own area mapping and cannot be recovered downstream of it.

Whether the primary omission contrast should pool the R-family (RXRR/RRXR/RRRX) with the global A/B-family (AAAX/AAXB/AXAB/BBBX/BBXA/BXBA) is not yet decided; they test different expectations (local/random vs global sequence structure) and the manuscript's own Introduction argues they should not be treated as equivalent.
